name: the_closed_file
conceit: An antiquarian card-catalogue drawer full of closed, filed portrait cards stands for every life already judged and shelved; ONE card lies apart, unfinished, on the desk, and only at the landing does its portrait turn to meet the viewer's eyes directly -- the device is a taxonomy the story then breaks.

anti: a single unrepeated event with no larger set or catalogue for the one card to stand apart from
a story whose turn is about MOTION or a physical journey, not about a filed record being reopened

plate_bill.must_contain: open wooden card-catalogue drawer, dozens of tabbed index cards standing closed and filed in tight ranks, a faint portrait-bust silhouette on each tab, lamplight, dust motes
one single index card lying flat and alone on the desk apart from the filed ranks, an unfinished ink portrait study of a calm bearded man occupying its upper half, dip pen and inkwell beside it
extreme close-up on one index card: a simple dignified ink portrait, three-quarter turned, eyes meeting the viewer directly, the card's lower portion bare, deep soft shadow around it

motion_slots.earned_by: the portrait turning to meet the viewer's eyes (P3) is the one beat worth animating in motion; the drawer and the desk card hold as $0 stills.

beat_template.hook: rank after rank of closed, filed cards, dense and slightly oppressive
beat_template.pivot: one unfiled card, unfinished, alone on the desk
beat_template.landing: the portrait turns, meets the viewer's own eyes

score_shape: a dry, ticking, orderly bed under the closed-drawer hook, thinning to a single held breath over the lone unfiled card, resolving to one warm sustained tone as the portrait turns and meets the eye.
